title.en: The Feels Guy lens
title.zh: 感同身受的梗图角度

paragraphs.en: Wojak is also known as Feels Guy, a reaction-image character used for recognisable feelings. This edition takes that limited expressive idea into ordinary hobby conversations. Choosing these responses suggests that acknowledging an experience appealed to you among the offered options. It does not establish sensitivity, loneliness, sadness, empathy or an accurate description of your emotional life.
paragraphs.zh: Wojak也常被称为Feels Guy，是表达熟悉感受的反应图角色。本版只把这个表达角度带进普通兴趣交流。选中这些回应，表示在提供的选项中，承认一种经历较吸引你，不确立敏感、孤独、难过、共情能力，也不准确描绘你的情绪生活。

title.en: A small reply after a rough attempt
title.zh: 尝试不顺后的一句小回应

paragraphs.en: A friend posts an uneven first craft attempt. You might say that you recognise the feeling of following a neat tutorial and making something quite different. That acknowledgement can make a conversation easier to enter. It need not claim that your experiences are identical, invite private disclosure or turn the friend’s post into a story about your own day.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友晒出不太整齐的第一次手工，你可以说自己懂照着漂亮教程却做出另一个样子的感觉。这能让交流容易开始一点，不必说双方经历完全相同，不必邀请隐私披露，也不用把对方的帖子变成自己的生活故事。

title.en: Five different ways a reply can work
title.zh: 另外五种回应怎样成立

paragraphs.en: Bloomer looks for a modest possibility; Doomer adds a dry, sceptical tone. Boomer reaches for a familiar favourite, Zoomer explores a new format, and NPC uses a repeatable routine. Feels Guy focuses on recognition. Any of those can communicate care or humour, and recognising a feeling does not give you privileged knowledge of what someone else needs.
paragraphs.zh: Bloomer找一点小可能，Doomer补上冷调质疑；Boomer回到熟悉喜好，Zoomer尝试新形式，NPC使用可重复流程。Feels Guy聚焦共鸣。这些方式都可能表达关心或幽默，而认出一种感受，并不代表自己更懂别人需要什么。

title.en: Where recognition can miss
title.zh: 共鸣也会错位

paragraphs.en: A person may want instructions, a laugh or simply to show the finished object. Saying that you know exactly how they feel could miss that purpose. If the exchange feels uncertain, ask what kind of response would be useful. These are possible communication choices, not a judgement that this result makes you emotionally perceptive or prone to overidentifying.
paragraphs.zh: 对方可能想要操作说明、一个笑话，或只是展示成品。说自己完全懂感受，也可能错过发帖目的。不确定时，可以问怎样回应比较有用。这只是沟通选择，不是在评这类结果的人情绪洞察强或容易过度代入。

title.en: Try a reply that leaves space
title.zh: 试一句留有空间的回应

paragraphs.en: For one low-stakes post, acknowledge a particular moment without claiming to understand the entire person. Then let them decide whether to continue the conversation. Notice whether your words fit what they actually shared. There is no need to tell a more personal story, become a public confidant or prove that you are the most relatable person in the thread.
paragraphs.zh: 挑一条轻松帖子，只承认其中一个具体瞬间，不声称理解整个人，再让对方决定是否继续聊。看看自己的话是否贴合对方实际分享的内容。不必讲更私人的故事，不必成为公开倾诉对象，也不必证明自己是帖子里最有共鸣的人。

title.en: The Bloomer lens
title.zh: 小步向前的梗图角度

paragraphs.en: Bloomer is an optimistic variant in Wojak meme culture. Here it supplies a limited editorial prompt: noticing one manageable possibility in an ordinary pastime. The selected options do not demonstrate optimism as a psychological trait, successful recovery, resilience or a better life than another result. This is a playful reading of choices, not a programme for changing your wellbeing.
paragraphs.zh: Bloomer在Wojak梗文化中常带乐观色彩。这里仅借它提示：在普通爱好里看见一个能做到的小可能。选择这些选项不证明心理特质上的乐观、康复、韧性，也不代表生活比其他结果更好。这是选择的娱乐读法，不是改善身心状况的方案。

title.en: A next attempt that fits
title.zh: 一次合适的下一步

paragraphs.en: Your hobby wish list has become too large to enjoy. Rather than promising a complete reinvention, you choose one small item that still interests you and leave the others undecided. That choice can make a pastime feel optional again. It is equally reasonable to stop, rest or choose another activity; the result creates no obligation to keep improving yourself.
paragraphs.zh: 兴趣清单已经大到不好玩了，不必许诺全面重启，可以挑一件仍感兴趣的小事，其余暂不决定。休闲就可能重新有选择感。停下、休息或换活动也同样合理；这一结果不产生持续提升自己的义务。

title.en: Possibility beside five other lenses
title.zh: 小可能与另外五个角度

paragraphs.en: Feels Guy acknowledges the experience, Doomer questions inflated promises and Boomer keeps an enjoyable old reference. Zoomer experiments with format; NPC makes participation repeatable. Bloomer asks what small option could be worth trying. Several can fit the same evening, and a constructive suggestion is not automatically more appropriate than recognition, a familiar favourite or a quiet routine.
paragraphs.zh: Feels Guy承认经历，Doomer质疑夸大承诺，Boomer保留喜欢的老参考；Zoomer试形式，NPC让参与可重复。Bloomer问的是哪一点小选择值得试。同一晚可以兼有好几种角度，建设性建议也不一定比共鸣、老爱好或安静流程更合适。

title.en: Do not turn possibility into pressure
title.zh: 别把可能变成压力

paragraphs.en: A small suggestion can still arrive when someone wants their frustration heard. You could accidentally imply that an unpleasant experience is easily fixed or that everyone should be looking forward. If that happens, check whether a suggestion was invited. The count cannot reveal a coping style, explain a person’s circumstances or support a claim that positivity causes better outcomes.
paragraphs.zh: 别人想让挫折被听见时，再小的建议也可能来得不合时宜。表达有时会像在说不快很容易解决，或人人都应该向前看。这时可确认对方是否想要建议。计数不能揭示应对风格、解释个人处境，也不能证明积极态度带来更好结果。

title.en: One optional, bounded trial
title.zh: 一次有范围、可选择的尝试

paragraphs.en: Choose one small hobby idea, decide how long you want to spend and give yourself permission not to continue. Afterwards record whether you enjoyed that actual attempt rather than whether it changed your life. This keeps the experiment close to the situation. It does not test whether you deserve the Bloomer name or need to replace any other result.
paragraphs.zh: 选一个兴趣小点子，决定愿意花多久，也允许自己不继续。结束后记下是否喜欢这一次，而不是有没有改变人生。这样尝试就贴近实际情境，不是在考自己配不配Bloomer，也不用拿它替换其他结果。

title.en: The Doomer lens
title.zh: 冷调旁观的梗图角度

paragraphs.en: Doomer has a bleak tone in Wojak meme culture. This edition deliberately limits its use to dry commentary and scepticism about overblown everyday claims. It does not assess depression, hopelessness, substance use, a political outlook or the future of your life. Selecting a wry response cannot establish the much broader and sometimes harmful stereotypes attached to the meme.
paragraphs.zh: Doomer在Wojak梗文化中常带灰暗语气。本版刻意把用法限于冷调评论，以及对日常夸大宣传的质疑，不评估抑郁、绝望、物质使用、政治观点或人生未来。选一句反讽，不能确立这个梗附带的更广泛甚至有害的刻板印象。

title.en: A hobby without a miracle headline
title.zh: 不带奇迹标题的爱好

paragraphs.en: A post claims that one tiny organisational trick will transform every creative session. Your preferred contribution might be a dry reminder that real materials, time and interruptions still exist. That can put a claim into proportion without deciding that nothing is worth doing. You can question the headline and still enjoy trying the small idea it contains.
paragraphs.zh: 帖子声称一个整理技巧能改变每次创作，你可能更想淡淡提醒，现实里的材料、时间和打断都还在。这可以给宣传一点尺度，不必得出什么都不值得做的结论。质疑标题，同时喜欢里面的小点子，也完全可以。

title.en: Dry humour beside five other options
title.zh: 冷幽默与另外五种选择

paragraphs.en: Feels Guy makes the experience recognisable; Bloomer identifies a modest possibility. Boomer recalls a familiar favourite, Zoomer tries a new format and NPC follows a usable routine. Doomer’s angle questions the grand claim. None of these proves who understands reality best, and a sceptical joke does not make another person’s enthusiasm foolish or your own response more intelligent.
paragraphs.zh: Feels Guy让经历有共鸣，Bloomer找一点小可能；Boomer想起老爱好，Zoomer试新形式，NPC照可用流程做。Doomer角度是质疑宏大宣传。这些都不能证明谁最懂现实；一个质疑玩笑不让别人的热情显得愚蠢，也不让自己的回应更聪明。

title.en: Aim the joke at the claim
title.zh: 让玩笑对准说法

paragraphs.en: A restrained comment about a promise can be different from mocking the person who liked it. In text, that difference may be hard to hear. If the exchange becomes unclear, explain the particular claim you were questioning and leave room for others to enjoy the activity. A count cannot tell whether your humour is welcome or whether someone else is oversensitive.
paragraphs.zh: 克制评论一项承诺，和嘲笑喜欢它的人并不相同，但文字里未必听得出来。交流不清楚时，可以说明自己质疑哪一句，也给别人享受活动的空间。计数看不出幽默是否受欢迎，更不能判断别人是不是过分敏感。

title.en: Try a concrete sceptical question
title.zh: 试一个具体的质疑问题

paragraphs.en: For one exaggerated hobby claim, replace a sweeping verdict with a specific question about time, materials or the promised outcome. Decide separately whether you want to try it. This is an experiment in keeping a conversation precise, not a requirement to become cheerful, stop joking or interpret an entertainment result as an explanation of how you feel.
paragraphs.zh: 遇到一次夸大的兴趣宣传，可以把全盘判断换成一个具体问题：时间、材料或承诺效果到底是什么？再另外决定要不要试。这是在尝试把交流说准，不要求变开朗、停止玩笑，也不把娱乐结果解释成自己的情绪成因。

This edition narrows it to enjoying a familiar reference or pastime. Selecting these options does not reveal your age, politics, technology ability or attitude toward younger people. A favourite can be old or simply familiar to you.
paragraphs.zh: Boomer Wojak在梗文化中带怀旧和世代戏仿意味，名称不能可靠说明出生年代。本版把它缩小为享受熟悉参考或爱好。选择这些选项不透露年龄、政治、技术能力或对年轻人的态度；喜好可以年代久，也可以只是自己已熟悉。

title.en: An old game with a present pleasure
title.zh: 老游戏里仍在发生的快乐

paragraphs.en: An old game comes up in conversation. You describe the part you still enjoy: a simple mechanic, an amusing sound or a memory of learning it with someone. That is different from declaring that everything newer is worse. The detail makes your preference understandable without asking the group to share a whole generation’s supposed taste.

paragraphs.en: Feels Guy names a recognisable experience; Bloomer finds a small possibility and Doomer questions an oversized claim. Zoomer tries a new format; NPC keeps the routine clear. Boomer revisits what remains enjoyable. Familiarity and novelty can fit the same person, while a repeated routine need not carry nostalgia. These distinctions describe the options here, not permanent categories of people.
paragraphs.zh: Feels Guy说出共鸣经历，Bloomer找一点可能，Doomer质疑大话；Zoomer试新形式，NPC保持清楚流程。Boomer重访仍喜欢的东西。同一个人可兼有熟悉与尝鲜，可重复流程也未必怀旧。这些区分描述本版选项，不给真人划永久类别。

title.en: A preference is not a universal standard
title.zh: 偏好不是普遍标准

paragraphs.en: A fond memory can lose its invitation when it becomes a test of whether someone knows the right reference. Others may enjoy the new version or have no history with either one. If a conversation stalls, explain the particular pleasure rather than asking them to defend their taste. The count cannot establish rigidity, wisdom or whether you are out of touch.
paragraphs.zh: 美好回忆如果变成考别人懂不懂正确老梗，就少了邀请感。别人可能喜欢新版，也可能两版都没接触。聊不下去时，可以说清具体乐趣，不要求对方为品味辩护。计数不能确立固执、智慧或是否脱离时代。

title.en: Share one detail, leave the comparison open
title.zh: 分享一处细节，让比较保持开放

paragraphs.en: Choose one familiar favourite and describe a detail that still works for you today. Invite someone to share their own example, which may be newer or entirely unrelated. Notice whether the exchange creates curiosity. There is no need to abandon your favourite, prove that it was objectively better or earn a fictional generational identity.
paragraphs.zh: 选一个熟悉喜好，讲一处今天仍让自己开心的细节，再邀请别人举自己的例子，较新或完全不同都行。看看交流能否带来好奇。不必抛弃老爱好、不必证明它客观更好，也不用争取某个虚构世代身份。

paragraphs.en: Zoomer Wojak is a meme caricature associated with Generation Z and newer cultural references. Here the name labels a much smaller editorial angle: trying an unfamiliar format in a low-stakes pastime. It does not infer your generation, age, appearance, music taste, attention span or digital competence. Someone of any age can be curious about a new way of making something.

title.en: A new format for an ordinary entry
title.zh: 给普通记录换个新形式

paragraphs.en: A hobby group introduces a new way to record a weekly attempt. You try one entry to discover what the format makes possible, without promising to move all your notes into it. The useful part is direct experience at a manageable scale. You may decide the familiar version works better and still have learned what you wanted from the trial.
paragraphs.zh: 兴趣小组推出新的每周记录方式，可以只试一条，看看这种格式能做什么，不必承诺把所有笔记都搬过去。可控范围内直接体验就有意义；试完觉得原来更好，也仍然弄明白了想知道的事。

title.en: Novelty beside five other contributions
title.zh: 尝鲜与另外五种贡献

paragraphs.en: Feels Guy looks for recognition, Bloomer for a small possibility and Doomer for proportion in a grand claim. Boomer keeps a familiar pleasure, while NPC keeps participation repeatable. Zoomer asks what the new format changes. You can use a novel format to express an old favourite or a regular routine, so the lenses do not form opposing generations or exclusive camps.
paragraphs.zh: Feels Guy找共鸣，Bloomer找小可能，Doomer给大话找尺度；Boomer保留熟悉快乐，NPC让参与可重复。Zoomer问新格式改变了什么。可以用新形式表达老爱好或固定日常，因此六角度不是对立世代或互斥阵营。

title.en: When experimenting becomes a demand
title.zh: 尝试变成要求的时候

paragraphs.en: A new format can be entertaining without being suitable for everyone. Others may need readable text, a familiar tool or time to decide. If a trial becomes a shared requirement, discuss what people actually need before moving further. This possible tradeoff does not mean the result identifies distraction, impulsivity or a personality that must constantly chase trends.
paragraphs.zh: 新格式好玩，也不一定适合每个人。别人可能需要清楚文字、熟悉工具或一点决定时间。尝试若变成共同要求，就先讨论实际需要，再往前走。这种取舍不代表结果识别出了分心、冲动或必须追潮流的人格。

title.en: Give one new format a small trial
title.zh: 给一种新格式一次小试用

paragraphs.en: Try a new format on something you would be comfortable discarding. Decide afterwards what it helped you express and whether you want to use it again. Keep the old version available if it still serves you. This is a reversible hobby experiment, not a test of whether you belong to a generation or understand the internet better than anyone else.
paragraphs.zh: 拿一件可以舍弃的小东西试新格式，之后再决定它帮助表达了什么、愿不愿继续用；旧版本仍有用就留着。这是能回头的兴趣尝试，不是测试属于哪一代，也不证明谁更懂互联网。

title.en: The NPC lens and its limits
title.zh: NPC梗图角度及其边界

paragraphs.en: NPC means non-player character in games. The Wojak meme has also been used to demean real people as unthinking; this quiz does not make that claim. This edition deliberately remixes the label into a limited, voluntary preference for a repeatable hobby routine. A result cannot establish intelligence, consciousness, an inner voice, independent thought or political conformity.
paragraphs.zh: NPC原指游戏里的非玩家角色；Wojak梗也被用来贬低真人缺乏思考，本测试不作这种判断。本版明确改写为一种有限、自愿的偏好：兴趣活动里可重复的流程。结果不能确立智力、意识、内心语言、独立思考或政治从众。

title.en: An ordinary check-in by choice
title.zh: 主动选择一次普通报到

paragraphs.en: A recurring hobby thread has a simple weekly format. You use it to record what you did without producing a new performance every time. Repetition can leave more room for the activity itself. Choosing that structure does not mean obeying it automatically: you can change it, stop posting or make a different decision when the circumstances change.
paragraphs.zh: 固定兴趣帖子每周格式简单，可以用来记录做过什么，不必次次重新表演。重复可能为活动本身留出空间。选择结构不等于自动服从；情境变了，仍可以改格式、暂停发帖或另作决定。

title.en: Routine beside five other lenses
title.zh: 流程与另外五个角度

paragraphs.en: Feels Guy recognises a feeling, Bloomer tries a small possibility and Doomer questions a large promise. Boomer revisits a favourite, while Zoomer explores a fresh format. NPC makes an ordinary action repeatable. A routine can hold any of those responses, and a familiar favourite need not become a schedule. None of the lenses measures whose life is more original or meaningful.
paragraphs.zh: Feels Guy认出感受，Bloomer试小可能，Doomer质疑大承诺；Boomer重访喜好，Zoomer探索新格式。NPC让普通行动可重复。流程可以容纳每一种回应，熟悉爱好也未必变成日程。六角度都不评谁的人生更原创或更有意义。

title.en: Review the routine rather than the person
title.zh: 检查流程，不给人下定义

paragraphs.en: A repeated step may stop serving the activity after the circumstances change. If that happens, ask what it is for now and whether you still want it. That is a practical question about a process, not evidence that you or anyone else lacks agency. Do not use this label as an insult or as a way to dismiss another person’s account of their experience.
paragraphs.zh: 情境变了，重复步骤可能不再服务活动。这时可问它现在有什么用途、自己是否仍想保留。这是对流程的实际提问，不是证明谁没有自主性。不要拿这个标签侮辱别人，或用它否定别人对自身经历的描述。

title.en: Keep, change or drop one step
title.zh: 保留、修改或放下一步

paragraphs.en: Pick one recurring hobby step and name the benefit you want from it. Decide deliberately to keep, modify or drop that step, then see whether the activity fits you better. You do not have to become more unusual to justify a routine. The point is exercising a choice, without letting a fictional label stand in for a real person.
paragraphs.zh: 挑兴趣活动里一个固定步骤，说清希望它带来什么，再主动决定保留、修改或放下，看看活动是否更适合自己。不必变得与众不同才有资格使用日常流程。重点是作出选择，不让虚构标签代替一个真实的人。

paragraphs.en: FermatMind independently authored this unofficial fan edition: every question, mapping, example and result. Its six named meme lenses are limited editorial remixes, not IDRlabs scores or an official Wojak taxonomy. Know Your Meme documents cultural usage and contested stereotypes; it provides neither a creator licence nor questionnaire validation. No source images, captions, questions or result text are reproduced. Names and associated works remain with their respective rights holders. The quiz infers no clinical condition, sex, gender role, age, ideology, intelligence, consciousness, inner speech, MBTI or career suitability. No result licenses insulting or dehumanising anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 费马独立创作本非官方同人版的全部题目、映射、例子与结果。六个命名角度是有限编辑改写，不是IDRlabs分数或官方Wojak分类。Know Your Meme记录文化用法及有争议的刻板印象，不提供创作者许可或题本验证。不复制来源图片、配文、题目或结果正文，名称及相关作品权利仍归相应权利人。本测试不推断临床状况、生理性别、性别角色、年龄、意识形态、智力、意识、内心语言、MBTI或职业适配；任何结果都不授权侮辱或非人化他人。
